components.name: Button
components.purpose: A button. `render` swaps its element but keeps a button's role, so a link that should look like a button is a `ButtonLink` instead.

components.name: ButtonGroup
components.purpose: A group of buttons, inputs or selects drawn as one control. Name it with `aria-label` when its purpose is not plain from its buttons. Groups nest, with a gap between them.

components.name: ButtonGroupSeparator
components.purpose: A line between a group's buttons, for groups whose buttons have no border of their own.

components.name: ButtonGroupText
components.purpose: Text inside a button group, such as a unit or a prefix, on the muted surface. `render` makes it another element, such as a `<label>` for the group's input.

components.name: ButtonLink
components.purpose: A link that looks like a Button: an `<a>`, or the element `render` names, with `data-slot="button"` so that it sits in a button group as a Button does, and its variant and size as `data-variant` and `data-size`.

components.name: Checkbox
components.purpose: A checkbox. Name it with a `<label>` around it or a `Label` whose `htmlFor` is its `id`. `indeterminate`, for a checkbox over others of which some are checked, fills the box and draws a dash in place of the check.

components.name: Combobox
components.purpose: A combobox: an input and the list it filters. Give it `items`, and render each in ComboboxList's child function; `multiple` chooses several, shown as ComboboxChips.

components.name: ComboboxCollection
components.purpose: A group's items, rendered by a child function, as ComboboxList renders the root's.

components.name: ComboboxContent
components.purpose: The popup that holds the list, under the input by default. Pass `anchor` from `useComboboxAnchor` to line it up with ComboboxChips.

components.name: ComboboxEmpty
components.purpose: What the popup says while no item matches, such as "No matches".

components.name: ComboboxGroup
components.purpose: Items under one ComboboxLabel.

components.name: ComboboxInput
components.purpose: The combobox's input inside an input group, with the button that opens the list (`showTrigger`, on by default) and the one that clears it (`showClear`). Name it with a `Label` whose `htmlFor` is its `id`, or `aria-label`.

components.name: ComboboxItem
components.purpose: One item, highlighted as the arrow keys reach it, with a check beside it while it is chosen.

components.name: ComboboxLabel
components.purpose: A heading for a ComboboxGroup's items.

components.name: ComboboxList
components.purpose: The list of matching items, which scrolls past 63 steps of the spacing scale.

components.name: ComboboxSeparator
components.purpose: A line between groups of items.

components.name: ComboboxTrigger
components.purpose: The button that opens the list, with a chevron after its content. Inside an input group it draws no background while pressed.

components.name: ComboboxValue
components.purpose: The chosen value as text, or a render function of the chosen items.

components.name: ComboboxChip
components.purpose: One chosen item as a chip, with a button that removes it (`showRemove`, on by default), named "Remove" and the chip's text when the chip is text.

components.name: ComboboxChips

props.description: The ref `useComboboxAnchor` returns, which lines the popup up with the chips.
props.name: ref

components.purpose: A multiple combobox's chosen items as chips, followed by its ComboboxChipsInput, in Input's outline.

components.name: ComboboxChipsInput
components.purpose: The input after a multiple combobox's chips.

components.name: Field
components.purpose: One field: a label, its control, and the field's description and error. Mark it `data-invalid` while its value is invalid.
components.example:
import { Field, FieldDescription, FieldGroup, FieldLabel, FieldLegend, FieldSet, Input } from "@basis/ui";

<FieldSet>
  <FieldLegend>Ticket</FieldLegend>
  <FieldGroup>
    <Field>
      <FieldLabel htmlFor="cusip">CUSIP</FieldLabel>
      <Input id="cusip" aria-describedby="cusip-help" />
      <FieldDescription id="cusip-help">Nine characters, check digit last.</FieldDescription>
    </Field>
  </FieldGroup>
</FieldSet>;

components.name: FieldContent
components.purpose: A horizontal field's label and description, stacked beside its control.

components.name: FieldDescription
components.purpose: A field's or fieldset's help text, in the muted colour.

components.name: FieldError
components.purpose: The field's errors in words, in the destructive colour, announced as they appear. Pass TanStack Form's `field.state.meta.errors` as `errors`, or the field's entry from `fieldErrors`; it shows one error as a line and several as a list, each message once, and nothing while there is no error. Its own `children` replace them.

components.name: FieldGroup
components.purpose: Fields stacked with the form's spacing. A `responsive` field lays its label beside its control once the group is wide enough.

components.name: FieldLabel
components.purpose: A field's `<label>`. Wrapping a whole `Field`, it becomes a choice card, tinted while its control is checked.

components.name: FieldLegend
components.purpose: A fieldset's `<legend>`. `variant="label"` sizes it as a label, for a set of checkboxes or radios.

components.name: FieldSeparator
components.purpose: A line between groups of fields, with optional text on it, such as "or".

components.name: FieldSet
components.purpose: A `<fieldset>`: a set of fields under one `FieldLegend`, such as a trade's settlement details.

components.name: FieldTitle
components.purpose: A title in a field's content that is not a `<label>`, such as a choice card's heading.

components.name: Input
components.purpose: A text input. With `aria-invalid` its outline turns the destructive colour; a `FieldError` beside it says why.

components.name: InputGroup
components.purpose: An input's outline holding the input and its addons. Name the input itself, with a `<label>` or `aria-label`.
components.example:
import { InputGroup, InputGroupAddon, InputGroupInput, InputGroupText } from "@basis/ui";

<InputGroup>
  <InputGroupInput aria-label="Notional" placeholder="0" />
  <InputGroupAddon align="inline-end">
    <InputGroupText>USD</InputGroupText>
  </InputGroupAddon>
</InputGroup>;

components.name: InputGroupAddon
components.purpose: Text, an icon or a button inside the group, before or after the input or on a line above or below it.

components.name: InputGroupButton
components.purpose: A button inside the group, such as a search or copy button, in Button's variants at the group's sizes. It is `type="button"` unless told otherwise, so it never submits the form by accident.

components.name: InputGroupInput
components.purpose: The group's input: an Input without its own outline.

components.name: InputGroupText
components.purpose: Text inside the group, such as a unit or a currency, in the muted colour.

components.name: InputGroupTextarea
components.purpose: The group's textarea: a Textarea without its own outline, with addons above or below it.

components.name: Label
components.purpose: A label. Point `htmlFor` at the control's `id`, or wrap the control in it.

components.name: NativeSelect
components.purpose: A native `<select>`. `className` places its wrapper; name it with a `Label` whose `htmlFor` is its `id`.

components.name: NativeSelectOptGroup
components.purpose: An `<optgroup>` of options under a label.

components.name: NativeSelectOption
components.purpose: One `<option>`.

components.name: RadioGroup
components.purpose: A set of radio items, one of which is chosen. Name it with `aria-labelledby` pointing at its legend or label.
components.example:
import { Field, FieldLabel, RadioGroup, RadioGroupItem } from "@basis/ui";

<RadioGroup defaultValue="buy" aria-label="Side">
  <Field orientation="horizontal">
    <RadioGroupItem id="side-buy" value="buy" />
    <FieldLabel htmlFor="side-buy">Buy</FieldLabel>
  </Field>
  <Field orientation="horizontal">
    <RadioGroupItem id="side-sell" value="sell" />
    <FieldLabel htmlFor="side-sell">Sell</FieldLabel>
  </Field>
</RadioGroup>;

components.name: RadioGroupItem
components.purpose: One choice in a RadioGroup, named by a `<label>` around it or a `Label` whose `htmlFor` is its `id`.

components.name: Select
components.purpose: A select: its trigger and its content, which holds the items. Give it `items` to show an item's label as the value, and `value` with `onValueChange`, or `defaultValue`.

components.name: SelectContent
components.purpose: The list that opens under the trigger, or over it with the chosen item aligned to it, the default.

components.name: SelectGroup
components.purpose: Items under one SelectLabel.

components.name: SelectItem
components.purpose: One option, with a check beside it while it is chosen.

components.name: SelectLabel
components.purpose: A heading for a SelectGroup's items.

components.name: SelectScrollDownButton
components.purpose: The arrow at the bottom of a list too long for the screen, which scrolls it down while hovered.

components.name: SelectScrollUpButton
components.purpose: The arrow at the top of a list too long for the screen, which scrolls it up while hovered.

components.name: SelectSeparator
components.purpose: A line between groups of items.

components.name: SelectTrigger
components.purpose: The button that opens the select, holding its SelectValue and a chevron. Name it with a `Label` whose `htmlFor` is its `id`, or `aria-label`.

components.name: SelectValue
components.purpose: The chosen item's label in the trigger, or its `placeholder` while nothing is chosen.

components.name: Slider
components.purpose: A slider. Give it `value` and `onValueChange`, or `defaultValue`; an array of two values draws a range. Name it with `aria-label`, which names each thumb.
components.example:
import { Slider } from "@basis/ui";

<Slider defaultValue={25} aria-label="Hedge ratio" />;

components.name: Switch
components.purpose: A switch that turns a setting on or off at once. Name it with a `<label>` around it or a `Label` whose `htmlFor` is its `id`. `size="sm"` draws a smaller track.

components.name: Textarea
components.purpose: A multi-line text input, at least 16 steps of the spacing scale tall, growing with its content.

components.name: Toggle
components.purpose: A toggle button, with `aria-pressed` while it is on. An icon-only toggle takes an `aria-label`.

components.name: ToggleGroup
components.purpose: A group of toggles in one look and size. `spacing` is the gap between them in steps of the spacing scale; at 0 they join into one control. Name the group with `aria-label`.

components.name: ToggleGroupItem
components.purpose: One toggle in a ToggleGroup, in the group's variant and size when the group sets them.

components.name: AlertDialog
components.purpose: An alert dialog: a dialog that asks the user to confirm or cancel an action. Unlike Dialog, a click outside does not close it; Escape and its cancel button do, and focus returns to the trigger.
components.example:
import {
  AlertDialog,
  AlertDialogAction,
  AlertDialogCancel,
  AlertDialogContent,
  AlertDialogDescription,
  AlertDialogFooter,
  AlertDialogHeader,
  AlertDialogTitle,
  AlertDialogTrigger,
  Button,
} from "@basis/ui";

<AlertDialog>
  <AlertDialogTrigger render={<Button variant="destructive" />}>Cancel order</AlertDialogTrigger>
  <AlertDialogContent>
    <AlertDialogHeader>
      <AlertDialogTitle>Cancel this order?</AlertDialogTitle>
      <AlertDialogDescription>The order leaves the book and cannot be restored.</AlertDialogDescription>
    </AlertDialogHeader>
    <AlertDialogFooter>
      <AlertDialogCancel>Keep it</AlertDialogCancel>
      <AlertDialogAction>Cancel order</AlertDialogAction>
    </AlertDialogFooter>
  </AlertDialogContent>
</AlertDialog>;

components.name: AlertDialogAction
components.purpose: The action the dialog confirms: a button drawn as a Button, which does not close the dialog by itself, so its handler closes it once the action has run.

components.name: AlertDialogCancel
components.purpose: The button that closes the dialog without acting, drawn as an outline Button unless `variant` says otherwise.

components.name: AlertDialogContent
components.purpose: The alert dialog's window, in a portal over the veil. `size="sm"` makes it narrow, with its text centred and its two actions side by side.

components.name: AlertDialogDescription
components.purpose: What the action does and what it cannot undo, which describes the dialog for assistive technology.

components.name: AlertDialogFooter
components.purpose: The actions, on a muted band across the dialog's foot: in a row at the end, or two equal columns when small.

components.name: AlertDialogHeader
components.purpose: The media, title and description: centred, and at the start at the default size on a wide screen.

components.name: AlertDialogMedia
components.purpose: An icon above the title, on a tile; it sizes the icon inside it. The tile is `secondary`, where shadcn's is `muted`, which in this theme's dark mode is the popover's own colour.

components.name: AlertDialogOverlay
components.purpose: The veil over the page behind an open alert dialog.

components.name: AlertDialogPortal
components.purpose: Renders the alert dialog's popup into the page's body, outside the trigger's layout. `AlertDialogContent` includes one.

components.name: AlertDialogTitle
components.purpose: The alert dialog's title, which names it for assistive technology.

components.name: AlertDialogTrigger
components.purpose: The control that opens the alert dialog; `render={<Button variant="destructive" />}` makes it a button.

components.name: Command

props.description: Whether the arrow keys wrap from the last item through the input to the first: true by default, as in Base UI, where cmdk's is false.
props.name: loop

components.purpose: A command menu: a CommandInput over a CommandList of CommandItems. The list narrows as the user types, the arrow keys move the highlight, and Enter or a click runs the highlighted item's `onSelect`. `label` names the menu for assistive technology, and `shouldFilter={false}` shows every item, for a list the app filters itself.
components.example:
import { Command, CommandEmpty, CommandGroup, CommandInput, CommandItem, CommandList } from "@basis/ui";

<Command label="Go to">
  <CommandInput placeholder="Search pages" />
  <CommandList>
    <CommandEmpty>No page matches.</CommandEmpty>
    <CommandGroup heading="Pages">
      <CommandItem onSelect={() => undefined}>Positions</CommandItem>
      <CommandItem onSelect={() => undefined}>Trades</CommandItem>
    </CommandGroup>
  </CommandList>
</Command>;

components.name: CommandEmpty
components.purpose: What the list shows when nothing matches the search, which assistive technology announces.

components.name: CommandGroup
components.purpose: Items under a `heading`, hidden while none of them matches the search.

components.name: CommandInput
components.purpose: The search box: a combobox that owns the list, in an InputGroup with a search icon. It takes the Command's `label` as its name unless given an `aria-label`; a placeholder says what to type.

components.name: CommandList
components.purpose: The list of items and groups, which scrolls past `max-h-72`. CommandEmpty may sit inside it.

components.name: CommandSeparator
components.purpose: A line between groups, hidden while the user searches unless `alwaysRender` is set.

components.name: CommandDialog

props.description: Adds a close button for assistive technology, which is hidden, since Escape closes the palette.
props.name: showCloseButton

components.purpose: The command palette: put a Command inside it. Escape and a click outside close it, and focus returns to the trigger. `title` and `description` name and describe it for assistive technology, and are not shown; `className` may set its width.

components.name: CommandItem

props.description: More words the item matches, such as `["preferences"]` for Settings.
props.name: keywords

props.description: Whether the item shows whatever the search.
props.name: forceMount

components.purpose: A command. It shows while its `value`, or else its text, or one of its `keywords` matches the search, and always with `forceMount`; Enter or a click runs `onSelect` with its value.

components.name: CommandShortcut
components.purpose: An item's keyboard shortcut, at its end. It only shows the shortcut; the app binds the keys.

components.name: ContextMenu
components.purpose: A context menu: actions on what is under the pointer, opened by a right click or a long press on its trigger, or by the keyboard's context-menu key or Shift+F10. Arrow keys move through its items, Enter or a click runs one, and Escape closes the menu.
components.example:
import { ContextMenu, ContextMenuContent, ContextMenuItem, ContextMenuTrigger } from "@basis/ui";

<ContextMenu>
  <ContextMenuTrigger>Right-click a position</ContextMenuTrigger>
  <ContextMenuContent>
    <ContextMenuItem onClick={() => undefined}>Allocate</ContextMenuItem>
    <ContextMenuItem onClick={() => undefined}>Copy CUSIP</ContextMenuItem>
  </ContextMenuContent>
</ContextMenu>;

components.name: ContextMenuCheckboxItem
components.purpose: An option that is on or off, with a check at its end when on.

components.name: ContextMenuContent
components.purpose: The menu's popup, in a portal, at the pointer.

components.name: ContextMenuGroup
components.purpose: Items that belong together, named by a ContextMenuLabel inside it.

components.name: ContextMenuItem
components.purpose: An action. `variant="destructive"` marks one that deletes or cannot be undone; `inset` lines it up with items that have an icon.

components.name: ContextMenuLabel
components.purpose: A group's heading, inside its ContextMenuGroup. `inset` lines it up with items that have an icon.

components.name: ContextMenuPortal
components.purpose: Renders the context menu's popup into the page's body. `ContextMenuContent` includes one.

components.name: ContextMenuRadioGroup
components.purpose: Options of which one is chosen, each a ContextMenuRadioItem.

components.name: ContextMenuRadioItem
components.purpose: One option of a ContextMenuRadioGroup, with a check at its end when chosen.

components.name: ContextMenuSeparator
components.purpose: A line between groups of a context menu's items.

components.name: ContextMenuShortcut
components.purpose: An item's keyboard shortcut, at its end. It only shows the shortcut; the app binds the keys.

components.name: ContextMenuSub
components.purpose: Holds a submenu: a ContextMenuSubTrigger and its ContextMenuSubContent.

components.name: ContextMenuSubContent
components.purpose: The submenu's popup, beside its trigger.

components.name: ContextMenuSubTrigger
components.purpose: The item that opens a submenu, on hover, a click, Enter or the right arrow key.

components.name: ContextMenuTrigger
components.purpose: The area a right click opens the menu on.

components.name: Dialog
components.purpose: A dialog: a window over the page that holds the user until it closes. Escape, a click outside and its close button close it, and focus returns to the trigger.
components.example:
import {
  Button,
  Dialog,
  DialogClose,
  DialogContent,
  DialogDescription,
  DialogFooter,
  DialogHeader,
  DialogTitle,
  DialogTrigger,
} from "@basis/ui";

<Dialog>
  <DialogTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Edit position</DialogTrigger>
  <DialogContent>
    <DialogHeader>
      <DialogTitle>Edit position</DialogTitle>
      <DialogDescription>Change the book this position sits in.</DialogDescription>
    </DialogHeader>
    <DialogFooter>
      <DialogClose render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Close</DialogClose>
    </DialogFooter>
  </DialogContent>
</Dialog>;

components.name: DialogClose
components.purpose: A control that closes the dialog; `render={<Button variant="outline" />}` makes it a button.

components.name: DialogContent
components.purpose: The dialog's window, in a portal over the veil, with a close button in its corner unless `showCloseButton` is false. `className` may set its width, such as `sm:max-w-lg`.

components.name: DialogDescription
components.purpose: A line under the title, which describes the dialog for assistive technology.

components.name: DialogFooter
components.purpose: The dialog's actions, on a muted band across its foot: stacked with the first last on a narrow screen, in a row at the end otherwise. `showCloseButton` adds a Close button.

components.name: DialogHeader
components.purpose: The dialog's title and description, stacked at its top.

components.name: DialogOverlay
components.purpose: The veil over the page behind an open dialog.

components.name: DialogPortal
components.purpose: Renders the dialog's popup into the page's body. `DialogContent` includes one.

components.name: DialogTitle
components.purpose: The dialog's title, which names it for assistive technology.

components.name: DialogTrigger
components.purpose: The control that opens the dialog; `render={<Button />}` makes it a button.

components.name: Drawer

props.description: Whether the panel shows a grip at its leading edge, which says it can be swiped.
props.name: showSwipeHandle

components.purpose: A drawer: a panel that slides in from an edge and can be swiped away, `down` by default. It is a dialog: Escape, a click outside and a swipe in `swipeDirection` close it, and focus returns to the trigger.
components.example:
import { Button, Drawer, DrawerContent, DrawerDescription, DrawerHeader, DrawerTitle, DrawerTrigger } from "@basis/ui";

<Drawer>
  <DrawerTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Show filters</DrawerTrigger>
  <DrawerContent>
    <DrawerHeader>
      <DrawerTitle>Filters</DrawerTitle>
      <DrawerDescription>Narrow the positions shown.</DrawerDescription>
    </DrawerHeader>
  </DrawerContent>
</Drawer>;

components.name: DrawerClose
components.purpose: A control that closes the drawer; `render={<Button variant="outline" />}` makes it a button.

components.name: DrawerContent
components.purpose: The panel, in a portal over the veil when the drawer is modal, against the edge its swipe direction points to.

components.name: DrawerDescription
components.purpose: The drawer's description, under its title, which screen readers announce with it.

components.name: DrawerFooter
components.purpose: The drawer's actions, at its foot.

components.name: DrawerHeader
components.purpose: The drawer's title and description, stacked at its top.

components.name: DrawerOverlay
components.purpose: The veil over the page behind a modal drawer.

components.name: DrawerPortal
components.purpose: Renders the drawer's popup into the page's body. `DrawerContent` includes one.

components.name: DrawerSwipeHandle
components.purpose: The grip at the panel's leading edge. It is decoration: the panel itself takes the swipe.

components.name: DrawerTitle
components.purpose: The drawer's title, which names it for assistive technology.

components.name: DrawerTrigger
components.purpose: The control that opens the drawer; `render={<Button />}` makes it a button.

components.name: DropdownMenu
components.purpose: A dropdown menu: a list of actions or options behind a button. Arrow keys move through its items, typing jumps to one, Enter or a click runs it, and Escape closes the menu and returns focus to the trigger.

components.name: DropdownMenuCheckboxItem
components.purpose: An option that is on or off, with a check at its end when on.

components.name: DropdownMenuContent
components.purpose: The menu's popup, in a portal, on the trigger's `side` (`bottom` by default), at least as wide as the trigger.

components.name: DropdownMenuGroup
components.purpose: Items that belong together, named by a DropdownMenuLabel inside it.

components.name: DropdownMenuItem
components.purpose: An action. `variant="destructive"` marks one that deletes or cannot be undone; `inset` lines it up with items that have an icon.

components.name: DropdownMenuLabel
components.purpose: A group's heading, inside its DropdownMenuGroup. `inset` lines it up with items that have an icon.

components.name: DropdownMenuPortal
components.purpose: Renders the dropdown menu's popup into the page's body. `DropdownMenuContent` includes one.

components.name: DropdownMenuRadioGroup
components.purpose: Options of which one is chosen, each a DropdownMenuRadioItem.

components.name: DropdownMenuRadioItem
components.purpose: One option of a DropdownMenuRadioGroup, with a check at its end when chosen.

components.name: DropdownMenuSeparator
components.purpose: A line between groups of a dropdown menu's items.

components.name: DropdownMenuShortcut
components.purpose: An item's keyboard shortcut, at its end. It only shows the shortcut; the app binds the keys.

components.name: DropdownMenuSub
components.purpose: Holds a submenu: a DropdownMenuSubTrigger and its DropdownMenuSubContent.

components.name: DropdownMenuSubContent
components.purpose: The submenu's popup, beside its trigger.

components.name: DropdownMenuSubTrigger
components.purpose: The item that opens a submenu, on hover, a click, Enter or the right arrow key.

components.name: DropdownMenuTrigger
components.purpose: The button that opens the menu. Render it as a Button, as in `render={<Button variant="outline" />}`.

components.name: HoverCard
components.purpose: A hover card: a preview of what a link leads to, shown while the pointer rests on the link or the link has keyboard focus. It is for sighted pointer users; what it shows must also be reachable by following the link.

components.name: HoverCardContent
components.purpose: The card, in a portal, on the trigger's `side` (`bottom` by default). `className` may set its width.

components.name: HoverCardTrigger
components.purpose: The link the card previews: an `<a>`, which takes `href`.

components.name: Menubar
components.purpose: A menubar: a row of menus, as at the top of a desktop application. The arrow keys move between its menus and through each one's items, and Escape closes the open menu and returns focus to its trigger.
components.example:
import { Menubar, MenubarContent, MenubarItem, MenubarMenu, MenubarTrigger } from "@basis/ui";

<Menubar>
  <MenubarMenu>
    <MenubarTrigger>File</MenubarTrigger>
    <MenubarContent>
      <MenubarItem onClick={() => undefined}>Export</MenubarItem>
    </MenubarContent>
  </MenubarMenu>
</Menubar>;

components.name: MenubarCheckboxItem
components.purpose: An option that is on or off, with a check at its start when on.

components.name: MenubarContent
components.purpose: The menu's popup, under its trigger.

components.name: MenubarGroup
components.purpose: A group of a menubar menu's items, which a `MenubarSeparator` sets apart from the next.

components.name: MenubarItem
components.purpose: An action. `variant="destructive"` marks one that deletes or cannot be undone; `inset` lines it up with items that have an icon.

components.name: MenubarLabel
components.purpose: A group's heading, inside its MenubarGroup. `inset` lines it up with items that have an icon.

components.name: MenubarMenu
components.purpose: One of the bar's menus: a MenubarTrigger and its MenubarContent.

components.name: MenubarPortal
components.purpose: Renders a menubar menu's popup into the page's body. `MenubarContent` includes one.

components.name: MenubarRadioGroup
components.purpose: Options of which one is chosen, each a MenubarRadioItem.

components.name: MenubarRadioItem
components.purpose: One option of a MenubarRadioGroup, with a check at its start when chosen.

components.name: MenubarSeparator
components.purpose: A line between groups of a menubar menu's items.

components.name: MenubarShortcut
components.purpose: An item's keyboard shortcut, at its end. It only shows the shortcut; the app binds the keys.

components.name: MenubarSub
components.purpose: Holds a submenu: a MenubarSubTrigger and its MenubarSubContent.

components.name: MenubarSubContent
components.purpose: The submenu's popup, beside its trigger.

components.name: MenubarSubTrigger
components.purpose: The item that opens a submenu, on hover, a click, Enter or the right arrow key.

components.name: MenubarTrigger
components.purpose: The menu's name in the bar, which opens it.

components.name: Popover
components.purpose: A popover: a panel anchored to its trigger, for a short form or details. Escape and a click outside close it, and focus moves into it and returns to the trigger.
components.example:
import { Button, Popover, PopoverContent, PopoverHeader, PopoverTitle, PopoverTrigger } from "@basis/ui";

<Popover>
  <PopoverTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Columns</PopoverTrigger>
  <PopoverContent>
    <PopoverHeader>
      <PopoverTitle>Columns shown</PopoverTitle>
    </PopoverHeader>
  </PopoverContent>
</Popover>;

components.name: PopoverContent
components.purpose: The panel, in a portal, on the trigger's `side` (`bottom` by default) at `sideOffset` pixels from it. `className` may set its width, such as `w-80`.

components.name: PopoverDescription
components.purpose: The popover's description, under its title.

components.name: PopoverHeader
components.purpose: The popover's title and description, stacked at its top.

components.name: PopoverTitle
components.purpose: The popover's title, which names it for assistive technology.

components.name: PopoverTrigger
components.purpose: The control that opens the popover; `render={<Button variant="outline" />}` makes it a button.

components.name: Sheet
components.purpose: A sheet: a panel over the page from one edge, for a form or details beside the current page. It is a dialog: Escape, a click outside and its close button close it, and focus returns to the trigger.
components.example:
import { Button, Sheet, SheetContent, SheetDescription, SheetHeader, SheetTitle, SheetTrigger } from "@basis/ui";

<Sheet>
  <SheetTrigger render={<Button variant="outline" />}>Trade details</SheetTrigger>
  <SheetContent>
    <SheetHeader>
      <SheetTitle>Trade details</SheetTitle>
      <SheetDescription>Bought 5,000 par at 99-16.</SheetDescription>
    </SheetHeader>
  </SheetContent>
</Sheet>;

components.name: SheetClose
components.purpose: A control that closes the sheet; `render={<Button variant="outline" />}` makes it a button.

components.name: SheetContent
components.purpose: The panel, in a portal over the veil, against the edge `side` names (`right` by default), with a close button in its corner unless `showCloseButton` is false.

components.name: SheetDescription
components.purpose: The sheet's description, under its title, which screen readers announce with it.

components.name: SheetFooter
components.purpose: The sheet's actions, at its foot.

components.name: SheetHeader
components.purpose: The sheet's title and description, stacked at its top.

components.name: SheetTitle
components.purpose: The sheet's title, which names it for assistive technology.

components.name: SheetTrigger
components.purpose: The control that opens the sheet; `render={<Button />}` makes it a button.

components.name: Tooltip
components.purpose: A tooltip: a short label for its trigger, shown while the pointer rests on it or it has keyboard focus. It names nothing for assistive technology, so an icon-only trigger still takes an `aria-label`.

components.name: TooltipContent
components.purpose: The label, in a portal, on the trigger's `side` (`top` by default), with an arrow pointing at the trigger.

components.name: TooltipProvider
components.purpose: Shares one delay among the tooltips inside it, so that after one opens its neighbours open at once. shadcn's default delay, 0, is kept.

components.name: TooltipTrigger
components.purpose: The element the tooltip describes; hovering or focusing it shows the tooltip.

components.name: Accordion
components.purpose: A stack of sections, each opened by its trigger. One opens at a time unless `multiple` is set.
components.example:
import { Accordion, AccordionContent, AccordionItem, AccordionTrigger } from "@basis/ui";

<Accordion>
  <AccordionItem value="terms">
    <AccordionTrigger>Terms</AccordionTrigger>
    <AccordionContent>Semi-annual coupon, 30/360.</AccordionContent>
  </AccordionItem>
</Accordion>;

components.name: AccordionContent
components.purpose: The section's content, a region named by its trigger, which fades in as it opens.

components.name: AccordionItem
components.purpose: One section: a trigger and the content it shows, with a line between it and the next.

components.name: AccordionTrigger
components.purpose: The section's heading: a button, named by its text, that Enter and Space open and close, with a chevron that points down when closed and up when open. Tab moves between the triggers: Base UI 1.9 dropped arrow-key focus between them, as the WAI-ARIA authoring practices did.

components.name: AspectRatio

props.description: Width over height, such as `16 / 9`.
props.name: ratio

components.purpose: A box whose height follows its width at `ratio`. Its content, such as an image, fills it with `size-full`.

components.name: Breadcrumb
components.purpose: The trail of links to the current page: a navigation landmark named "breadcrumb".
components.example:
import {
  Breadcrumb,
  BreadcrumbItem,
  BreadcrumbLink,
  BreadcrumbList,
  BreadcrumbPage,
  BreadcrumbSeparator,
} from "@basis/ui";

<Breadcrumb>
  <BreadcrumbList>
    <BreadcrumbItem>
      <BreadcrumbLink href="/bonds">Bonds</BreadcrumbLink>
    </BreadcrumbItem>
    <BreadcrumbSeparator />
    <BreadcrumbItem>
      <BreadcrumbPage>US91282CRF04</BreadcrumbPage>
    </BreadcrumbItem>
  </BreadcrumbList>
</Breadcrumb>;

components.name: BreadcrumbEllipsis
components.purpose: Stands for the items left out of a long trail, often as a menu's trigger.

components.name: BreadcrumbItem
components.purpose: One step of the trail: a `BreadcrumbLink`, or the `BreadcrumbPage` for the current page.

components.name: BreadcrumbLink
components.purpose: A link to an earlier page: an `<a>`, or the router's link through `render`, as in `<BreadcrumbLink render={<Link to="/desks" />}>Desks</BreadcrumbLink>`.

components.name: BreadcrumbList
components.purpose: The ordered list of the trail's items and separators.

components.name: BreadcrumbPage
components.purpose: The current page, which is not a link: marked `aria-current="page"`. shadcn also gives it `role="link"` and `aria-disabled`, which announce a link that cannot be followed or focused; it is plain text here.

components.name: BreadcrumbSeparator
components.purpose: The mark between two items, a chevron unless it is given children. Assistive technology skips it.

components.name: Card
components.purpose: A card: a raised panel on the `card` surface. `size="sm"` tightens its spacing.
components.example:
import { Card, CardContent, CardDescription, CardHeader, CardTitle, Money } from "@basis/ui";

<Card>
  <CardHeader>
    <CardTitle>Market value</CardTitle>
    <CardDescription>At yesterday's close</CardDescription>
  </CardHeader>
  <CardContent>
    <Money value={1_234_567.89} />
  </CardContent>
</Card>;

components.name: CardAction
components.purpose: A control at the header's end, such as a menu button, beside the title and description.

components.name: CardContent
components.purpose: The card's body.

components.name: CardDescription
components.purpose: A line under the card's title saying what the card shows.

components.name: CardFooter
components.purpose: The card's last row, for its actions or a note.

components.name: CardHeader
components.purpose: The card's title, description and action. With an action, the action takes a column of its own at the end.

components.name: CardTitle
components.purpose: The card's title.

components.name: Collapsible
components.purpose: A section that shows and hides its content. `open` and `onOpenChange` control it, or `defaultOpen` starts it.

components.name: CollapsibleContent
components.purpose: What the collapsible shows when open and hides when closed.

components.name: CollapsibleTrigger
components.purpose: The button that opens and closes the content, with `aria-expanded` and `aria-controls` set. Enter and Space toggle it, as on any button.

components.name: Item
components.purpose: One item: a `<div>`, or the element `render` names, such as a link, with its variant and size as `data-variant` and `data-size`.
components.example:
import { Button, Item, ItemActions, ItemContent, ItemDescription, ItemTitle } from "@basis/ui";

<Item variant="outline">
  <ItemContent>
    <ItemTitle>Rates book</ItemTitle>
    <ItemDescription>42 positions</ItemDescription>
  </ItemContent>
  <ItemActions>
    <Button size="sm" variant="outline">
      Open
    </Button>
  </ItemActions>
</Item>;

components.name: ItemActions
components.purpose: The item's buttons, at its end.

components.name: ItemContent
components.purpose: The item's title and description, which take the room the media and actions leave.

components.name: ItemDescription
components.purpose: The item's description, cut at two lines.

components.name: ItemFooter
components.purpose: A row across the item's full width, below its content.

components.name: ItemGroup
components.purpose: A stack of items, with a gap that follows its items' size. shadcn gives it `role="list"`, which requires children with the `listitem` role that an item, often a link, cannot take, so it is a plain group here.

components.name: ItemHeader
components.purpose: A row across the item's full width, above its content.

components.name: ItemMedia
components.purpose: The item's icon or image, at its start.

components.name: ItemSeparator
components.purpose: A line between two items in a group.

components.name: ItemTitle
components.purpose: The item's title, on one line.

components.name: NavigationMenu
components.purpose: A site's top-level navigation: a navigation landmark holding a NavigationMenuList. `align` places the popup against the list.
components.example:
import {
  NavigationMenu,
  NavigationMenuContent,
  NavigationMenuItem,
  NavigationMenuLink,
  NavigationMenuList,
  NavigationMenuTrigger,
} from "@basis/ui";

<NavigationMenu>
  <NavigationMenuList>
    <NavigationMenuItem>
      <NavigationMenuTrigger>Books</NavigationMenuTrigger>
      <NavigationMenuContent>
        <NavigationMenuLink href="/books/rates">Rates</NavigationMenuLink>
        <NavigationMenuLink href="/books/credit">Credit</NavigationMenuLink>
      </NavigationMenuContent>
    </NavigationMenuItem>
  </NavigationMenuList>
</NavigationMenu>;

components.name: NavigationMenuContent
components.purpose: What a trigger opens, shown in the popup. It slides a step in from the side of the item opened.

components.name: NavigationMenuIndicator
components.purpose: A small arrow below the item whose menu is open.

components.name: NavigationMenuItem
components.purpose: One top-level item: a trigger and its content, or a link.

components.name: NavigationMenuLink
components.purpose: A link, in a menu's content or, with `variant="trigger"`, in the top-level list beside the triggers. `active` marks the current page with `aria-current="page"`, and `render` makes it the router's link component.

components.name: NavigationMenuList
components.purpose: The row of the navigation menu's items.

components.name: NavigationMenuPositioner
components.purpose: Where the menus' popup opens: below the list, at its start by default. NavigationMenu renders one already.

components.name: NavigationMenuTrigger
components.purpose: The button that opens its item's content, named by its text, with a chevron that turns over while it is open.

components.name: Pagination
components.purpose: The pages' links: a navigation landmark named "pagination".
components.example:
import {
  Pagination,
  PaginationContent,
  PaginationItem,
  PaginationLink,
  PaginationNext,
  PaginationPrevious,
} from "@basis/ui";

<Pagination>
  <PaginationContent>
    <PaginationItem>
      <PaginationPrevious href="?page=1" />
    </PaginationItem>
    <PaginationItem>
      <PaginationLink href="?page=2" isActive>
        2
      </PaginationLink>
    </PaginationItem>
    <PaginationItem>
      <PaginationNext href="?page=3" />
    </PaginationItem>
  </PaginationContent>
</Pagination>;

components.name: PaginationContent
components.purpose: The row of the pagination's items.

components.name: PaginationEllipsis
components.purpose: Stands for the pages left out between two links. Assistive technology skips it.

components.name: PaginationItem
components.purpose: One item of the pagination: a link, the previous or next link, or an ellipsis.

components.name: PaginationLink

props.description: Whether the link is to the page shown, which it marks with `aria-current="page"` and the outline look.
props.name: isActive

props.description: Button's size; `icon` by default, a square for a page number.
props.name: size

components.purpose: A link to one page, drawn as a ghost ButtonLink, or an outline one for the page shown.

components.name: PaginationNext

props.description: Whether the link is to the page shown, which it marks with `aria-current="page"` and the outline look.
props.name: isActive

props.description: Button's size; `icon` by default, a square for a page number.
props.name: size

components.purpose: The link to the next page, named "Go to next page". Its text shows from the `sm` breakpoint up.

components.name: PaginationPrevious

props.description: Whether the link is to the page shown, which it marks with `aria-current="page"` and the outline look.
props.name: isActive

props.description: Button's size; `icon` by default, a square for a page number.
props.name: size

components.purpose: The link to the previous page, named "Go to previous page". Its text shows from the `sm` breakpoint up.

components.name: ResizableHandle

props.description: Draws a grip on the line.
props.name: withHandle

props.description: Stops this handle from resizing its panels.
props.name: disabled

components.purpose: The handle between two panels: a focusable separator, which an app names with `aria-label`, such as "Resize the trade list". Drag it, or focus it and use the arrow keys, Home and End.

components.name: ResizablePanel

props.description: Names the panel in a stored layout and in its handle's `aria-controls`; generated when left out.
props.name: id

props.description: Its starting size, in percent; without one it shares what the other panels leave.
props.name: defaultSize

props.description: The smallest it may be, in percent; 0 by default.
props.name: minSize

props.description: The largest it may be, in percent; 100 by default.
props.name: maxSize

components.purpose: A panel of a ResizablePanelGroup, which must be one of the group's own children.

components.name: ResizablePanelGroup

props.description: `horizontal` puts the panels side by side, `vertical` stacks them.
props.name: orientation

props.description: The sizes to start from, by panel `id`, such as a layout `onLayoutChanged` stored. Read once, on mount.
props.name: defaultLayout

props.description: Called with the new layout when a drag ends or a key moves a handle: the time to store it.
props.name: onLayoutChanged

props.description: Stops every handle in the group from resizing.
props.name: disabled

components.purpose: A group of panels split by handles, filling its parent. Give each panel an `id` when its layout is stored.

components.name: ScrollArea
components.purpose: A region that scrolls its content with a thin scrollbar of the theme's own, vertical by default. Give it a height, such as `h-72`, and it scrolls what overflows. Add a horizontal `ScrollBar` for content wider than it.

components.name: ScrollBar
components.purpose: A scrollbar for a `ScrollArea`, vertical by default; `ScrollArea` already holds a vertical one.

components.name: Separator
components.purpose: A line between groups of content, horizontal by default. Screen readers announce it as a separator.

components.name: Sidebar

props.description: `sidebar` sits against the page's edge, `floating` is a raised panel, `inset` sets the page in a panel.
props.name: variant

props.description: `offcanvas` slides it away, `icon` folds it to its icons, `none` keeps it open.
props.name: collapsible

components.purpose: The app's sidebar, for its navigation. It folds by `collapsible`, and is a sheet below the `md` breakpoint.

components.name: SidebarInset
components.purpose: The page beside the sidebar, its `<main>`, or the element `render` names where the page already has one. With the inset variant it sits in a raised panel.

components.name: SidebarProvider

props.description: Whether the sidebar starts open when the cookie holds no choice yet; `true` by default.
props.name: defaultOpen

props.description: Whether the sidebar is open, when the app controls it.
props.name: open

components.purpose: Holds the sidebar's state for the Sidebar, its trigger and `useSidebar`, and lays the sidebar and the page's SidebarInset out side by side. Ctrl+B or Cmd+B toggles the sidebar, and the `basis-ui-sidebar` cookie keeps the choice for a week.

components.name: SidebarRail
components.purpose: A thin strip along the sidebar's edge that toggles it when clicked, for the pointer. It is out of the tab order, and narrower than the 24 px target, as shadcn draws it: SidebarTrigger and the shortcut do the same, which is WCAG 2.2's exception for a target with an equivalent.

components.name: SidebarTrigger
components.purpose: The button that opens and closes the sidebar, named "Toggle Sidebar".

components.name: SidebarContent
components.purpose: The sidebar's scrolling middle, between its header and footer.

components.name: SidebarFooter
components.purpose: The sidebar's bottom row, under its content, for the user menu or settings.

components.name: SidebarHeader
components.purpose: The sidebar's top row, over its content, for the app's name.

components.name: SidebarInput
components.purpose: A search or filter field in the sidebar, with the Input's look on the page's background.

components.name: SidebarSeparator
components.purpose: A line between the sidebar's sections, in the sidebar's border colour.

components.name: SidebarGroup
components.purpose: A group of the sidebar's content, with an optional `SidebarGroupLabel`.

components.name: SidebarGroupAction
components.purpose: A button beside the group's label, such as one that adds an item; name it with `aria-label` or `sr-only` text.

components.name: SidebarGroupContent
components.purpose: The body of a sidebar group, under its label.

components.name: SidebarGroupLabel
components.purpose: The group's heading, hidden on the icon rail.

components.name: SidebarMenu
components.purpose: A list of the sidebar's menu items.
components.example:
import {
  Sidebar,
  SidebarContent,
  SidebarGroup,
  SidebarGroupContent,
  SidebarGroupLabel,
  SidebarInset,
  SidebarMenu,
  SidebarMenuButton,
  SidebarMenuItem,
  SidebarProvider,
  SidebarTrigger,
} from "@basis/ui";

<SidebarProvider>
  <Sidebar>
    <SidebarContent>
      <SidebarGroup>
        <SidebarGroupLabel>Books</SidebarGroupLabel>
        <SidebarGroupContent>
          <SidebarMenu>
            <SidebarMenuItem>
              <SidebarMenuButton isActive render={<a href="/positions" />}>
                Positions
              </SidebarMenuButton>
            </SidebarMenuItem>
          </SidebarMenu>
        </SidebarGroupContent>
      </SidebarGroup>
    </SidebarContent>
  </Sidebar>
  <SidebarInset>
    <SidebarTrigger />
  </SidebarInset>
</SidebarProvider>;

components.name: SidebarMenuAction

props.description: Shows the action only while its item is hovered or focused, from the `md` breakpoint up.
props.name: showOnHover

components.purpose: A button at the end of a menu item, such as one that opens the item's menu; name it with `aria-label`.

components.name: SidebarMenuBadge
components.purpose: A count or short label at the end of a menu item.

components.name: SidebarMenuItem
components.purpose: One item of a sidebar menu, holding a `SidebarMenuButton` and, optionally, a submenu.

components.name: SidebarMenuSkeleton

props.description: Draws an icon's place before the text.
props.name: showIcon

components.purpose: A menu item's place while the menu loads.

components.name: SidebarMenuSub
components.purpose: A menu item's sub-menu, indented under it and hidden on the icon rail.

components.name: SidebarMenuSubButton

props.description: Marks the link as the current page's, with `data-active`.
props.name: isActive

components.purpose: A sub-menu's link: an `<a>`, or the router's link through `render`.

components.name: SidebarMenuSubItem
components.purpose: One item of a sidebar submenu, holding a `SidebarMenuSubButton`.

components.name: SidebarMenuButton

props.description: Marks the button as the current page's, with `data-active`.
props.name: isActive

props.description: What names the button on the folded rail: its text, or TooltipContent's props.
props.name: tooltip

components.purpose: A menu's button, or its link through `render`, as in `<SidebarMenuButton render={<Link to="/trades" />}>`.

components.name: Tabs
components.purpose: A set of panels shown one at a time, horizontal by default. `defaultValue` or `value` names the open tab.
components.example:
import { Tabs, TabsContent, TabsList, TabsTrigger } from "@basis/ui";

<Tabs defaultValue="positions">
  <TabsList>
    <TabsTrigger value="positions">Positions</TabsTrigger>
    <TabsTrigger value="trades">Trades</TabsTrigger>
  </TabsList>
  <TabsContent value="positions">42 positions</TabsContent>
  <TabsContent value="trades">7 trades today</TabsContent>
</Tabs>;

components.name: TabsContent
components.purpose: The panel a trigger opens, a tabpanel named by its trigger.

components.name: TabsList
components.purpose: The row of triggers, a tablist. `variant="line"` underlines the active trigger instead of raising it.

components.name: TabsTrigger
components.purpose: A tab, named by its text, that opens the panel with the same `value`.

components.name: Alert
components.purpose: A callout: an optional icon first, then an AlertTitle, an AlertDescription and an AlertAction. A status variant pairs its colour with an icon, such as `CircleCheckIcon` for `success`.

components.name: AlertAction
components.purpose: A control in the alert's top right corner, such as a Button that dismisses it.

components.name: AlertDescription
components.purpose: The alert's text, under its title.

components.name: AlertTitle
components.purpose: The alert's title, which also names it.

components.name: Avatar
components.purpose: A person's picture or initials in a circle: 32 px, or 24 px at `size="sm"` and 40 px at `size="lg"`.

components.name: AvatarBadge
components.purpose: A dot at the avatar's bottom right, such as a presence indicator; an icon inside it shows from the default size.

components.name: AvatarFallback
components.purpose: What shows until the picture loads, or in its place: usually the person's initials.

components.name: AvatarGroup
components.purpose: Avatars overlapping in a row, each ringed in the background colour.

components.name: AvatarGroupCount
components.purpose: The count of avatars a group leaves out, such as "+3", at the size of the group's avatars.

components.name: AvatarImage
components.purpose: The picture, shown once it has loaded. Its `alt` names the person.

components.name: Badge
components.purpose: A badge: a `<span>`, or the element `render` names, with `data-slot="badge"` and its variant as `data-variant`.
components.example:
import { Badge } from "@basis/ui";

<Badge variant="secondary">Settled</Badge>;

components.name: Empty
components.purpose: An empty state, centred in the space it fills: EmptyHeader, then EmptyContent for what to do next. `outline` draws a dashed border round it.
components.example:
import { Button, Empty, EmptyContent, EmptyDescription, EmptyHeader, EmptyTitle } from "@basis/ui";

<Empty>
  <EmptyHeader>
    <EmptyTitle>No trades today</EmptyTitle>
    <EmptyDescription>Trades booked today show here.</EmptyDescription>
  </EmptyHeader>
  <EmptyContent>
    <Button variant="outline">Book a trade</Button>
  </EmptyContent>
</Empty>;

components.name: EmptyContent
components.purpose: What the user can do next, such as a Button that clears the filters.

components.name: EmptyDescription
components.purpose: A line under the empty state's title saying why it is empty and what to do.

components.name: EmptyHeader
components.purpose: The media, title and description.

components.name: EmptyMedia
components.purpose: An illustration, or an icon on a tile with `variant="icon"`.

components.name: EmptyTitle
components.purpose: The empty state's title.

components.name: Kbd
components.purpose: A key, such as `Ctrl` or `K`, in a `<kbd>` element. An icon inside it is sized to the key.

components.name: KbdGroup
components.purpose: Keys pressed together, such as `Ctrl` `K`: a `<kbd>` holding a Kbd for each key, as HTML nests them.

components.name: Progress
components.purpose: A progress bar: its children, such as a label and the value, above a full-width track. `value` is out of `max`, 100 by default, and `null` makes it indeterminate.

components.name: ProgressIndicator
components.purpose: The filled part of the progress bar's track. `Progress` includes it.

components.name: ProgressLabel
components.purpose: The bar's name, which labels the `progressbar`.

components.name: ProgressTrack
components.purpose: The progress bar's track. `Progress` includes it.

components.name: ProgressValue
components.purpose: The value as text, such as "40%", at the end of the label's line, in tabular figures.

components.name: Skeleton
components.purpose: A placeholder block. `className` gives it the size of what it stands for, such as `h-4 w-32`, or `size-8` with `variant="circle"` for an avatar.
components.example:
import { Skeleton } from "@basis/ui";

<Skeleton className="h-4 w-32" />;

import { Spinner } from "@basis/ui";

<Spinner />;

components.name: TableCaption
components.purpose: The table's caption, which names it for screen readers.

components.name: TableCell
components.purpose: A cell; `variant="numeric"` for a number, so the column's digits line up.

components.name: TableFooter
components.purpose: The totals row or rows, on a muted band below the body.

components.name: TableHead
components.purpose: A column heading; `variant="numeric"` for a column of numbers.

components.name: TableHeader
components.purpose: The table's header row group, holding its `TableHead` cells.

components.name: TableRow

components.name: ToastClose

components.purpose: A toast's text and action, inside the toast.

components.name: TypographyH3

components.name: TypographyH4

props.description: Colour a gain `gain` and a loss `loss`, and write a plus sign before a gain.

components.name: Num

props.description: Colour a gain `gain` and a loss `loss`, and write a plus sign before a gain.

components.example:
import { Bps, Money, Num, Pct, Price32 } from "@basis/ui";

<Num value={1234.5} decimals={2} />; // 1,234.50
<Num value={-1250.5} signed />; // -1,250.50, in the loss colour
<Money value={2_500_000_000} abbreviate="B" />; // $2.5B
<Pct value={0.0525} />; // 5.25%: rates are fractions
<Bps value={0.0025} />; // 25.00 bp; decimals={0} shows 25 bp
<Price32 value={99.515625} />; // 99-16+
